title: Game Difficulty
story: You're building a puzzle game and need configurable difficulty levels. Easy mode gives 10 attempts, Medium gives 5, Hard gives 3, Expert gives 1. The settings screen needs to show descriptions like "For beginners" or "You will cry" based on the selected level.
why: Difficulty enums with numeric thresholds and string descriptions are the foundation of every game's settings system.
analogy: Difficulty is the "game slider" in the settings menu. Easy is training wheels � lots of tries. Expert is the tightrope with no net � one attempt. The description is the warning label under each level.
try_it: Add a `Nightmare` difficulty mode with 0 attempts (instant game over on error). Add a `Difficulty.score_multiplier(self) -> Float64` method (Easy = 0.5x, Medium = 1.0x, Hard = 2.0x, Expert = 5.0x).
tips: Each match arm returns a different constant � no shared calculation needed
Keep descriptions flavorful � they're player-facing text, not just variable names
Use numeric values that feel right: Easy(10), Medium(5), Hard(3), Expert(1) has a satisfying curve
common_mistakes: Mixing up the order of match arms � the enum order in match must follow the definition order
Forgetting to make `Expert` the hardest (fewest attempts) � the progression should get harder
